cf.title: Fix LSN of logical decoding message

input.subject: Why is the LSN reported for pg_logical_emit_message() different from other decoded operations?

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated with a reproducible case and a field report of a lost INSERT in Debezium (message #1). The review notes say reviewers accept the master-only change with documentation fixes in the back branches (messages #10 to #13). Confidence is medium because only 3 of 13 messages and no code were read.

brief.title: Report start LSN for transactional logical decoding messages
brief.problem: Logical decoding reports a logical message at the end LSN of its WAL record, but INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE use the start LSN. A transactional message can then share the LSN of the next change. Debezium resumed after a crash at such an LSN, treated the following INSERT as processed and lost it.
brief.proposed_design: On master, decode.c queues transactional messages with origptr (start LSN) and keeps endptr for non-transactional messages, which receivers handle as separate transactions. The back branches keep the current behavior, and their documentation now says the end LSN is reported. The behavior change is to be described in the commit message for the release notes.
user_visible_surface: LSN reported for transactional messages in pg_logical_slot_get_changes() and the logical replication protocol Message changes from end to start of the WAL record.
The message_lsn argument of the LogicalDecodeMessageCB output plugin callback changes the same way.
The protocol.sgml text for the Message LSN field now distinguishes transactional and non-transactional messages.
Back branches 14 to 19 get a documentation change that says the Message LSN is the end LSN.
author_claims: The current behavior contradicts the documentation and can cause data loss in consumers that resume from persisted change LSNs.
Postgres itself does not use this LSN, so there is no correctness problem in core.
Debezium can accommodate a fix in either a minor or a major release.
Fujitsu confirmed its proprietary Userlog Operation is not affected.
Few consumers likely have special handling for message LSNs today.
brief.thread_state: Sawada, Horiguchi, Nagata, Kuroda, solai v and João Rito replied, and all accept the master-only fix with doc changes in back branches. Open requests are more code comments on the non-transactional case, a matching update to message_cb text in logicaldecoding.sgml, and a regression test that tells old and new behavior apart.
unclear: No v3 patch updates logicaldecoding.sgml, which still says the lsn is the WAL location of the message.
No test covers the change, and nobody tested the non-transactional case or the back-branch patches.
The proposal does not say how other plugins or tools that store message_lsn, such as pgoutput subscribers, handle the change on upgrade to 20.
The v3 patch does not say whether the v1 change to 020_messages.pl was kept or dropped.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: decode.c changes which LSN logical decoding reports for transactional messages; the WAL record itself does not change.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: The Message LSN field in the logical replication protocol changes meaning for transactional messages, per the protocol.sgml hunk.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The message_lsn argument of the LogicalDecodeMessageCB output plugin callback changes from end LSN to start LSN for transactional messages.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The code change is master-only; branches 14 to 19 get a protocol.sgml correction that says the end LSN is reported.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The Message LSN now has two meanings, start for transactional and end for non-transactional, which documentation and plugins must keep straight.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Will the next version update the message_cb text in logicaldecoding.sgml, which still says the lsn is the WAL location of the message?
Which regression test tells the old and new LSN apart for a transactional message, and which one covers the non-transactional case?
What happens to a consumer that stored a transactional message's end LSN on 19 and resumes from it after upgrade to 20?
Does v3 keep or drop the v1 change to 020_messages.pl?
Were the back-branch documentation patches for 14 and for 15 to 19 checked against each branch's actual behavior?

committability.owner_note: The review notes say Sawada shaped the transactional/non-transactional split in message #10 and agreed to own it in message #12; those messages were not shown here.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behavior change in the logical replication protocol and the output plugin callback in 20, and for any external consumer that depended on the end LSN.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted three patch versions and moved the entry to the current CommitFest on 2026-11-03.

priority.reason: The patch touches decode.c and protocol.sgml only and fixes a data-loss case reported for Debezium. It affects users of logical decoding who emit transactional messages, and the remaining requests are documentation, comments and a test.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so it could not be checked that pgoutput and test_decoding pass the new value through the same way. Messages #4 to #13 are known here only through the brief and the review notes.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert logical snapshot filename format change in SnapBuildSnapshotExists().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert logical snapshot filename format change in SnapBuildSnapshotExists().
Reverted commit(s): Standardize LSN formatting by zero padding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 2633dae2e48 standardized LSN formatting but mistakenly changed
the logical snapshot filename format in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() from
"%X-%X.snap" to "%08X-%08X.snap". Other code still used the original
"%X-%X.snap" format, causing the replication slot synchronization worker
to fail to find existing snapshot files and produce excessive log messages.

This commit restores the original "%X-%X.snap" format
in SnapBuildSnapshotExists() to resolve the issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical decoding on standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: Logical decoding on standby

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical Decoding with timelines
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical decoding in the walsender follow timeline changes, as physical replication does, so that logical replication can cascade from a standby. It moved the walsender's send-pointer and timeline logic into shared functions used by both physical and logical sending.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs, the author, withdrew it as Returned with Feedback and said he had a new approach for the next release. Andres Freund noted that it covers only the walsender, while logical decoding also runs through SQL functions. He also said it does not let decoding start on a standby, which also needs forced hot_standby_feedback and slot cleanup in dbase_redo. Michael Paquier reported that the patch no longer applied, the earlier review comments were unaddressed, and no tests were shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Afaics the patch as is won't allow to start logical decoding on a standby.

precedents_retrieved.title: Filter irrelevant change before reassemble transactions during logical decoding
precedents_retrieved.authors: Jie Li (adger), Ajin Cherian (ajinc), Zhijie Hou (houzj)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Filter out changes for relations the output plugin does not publish while decoding, before they are queued into the reorder buffer, so they are never spilled to disk. A new output plugin callback (filter_change) decides per relation, with a relfilelocator hash table and a pause of filtering after unfilterable changes to limit overhead.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No visible message records the withdrawal decision. Amit Kapila first warned that per-change catalog lookups add overhead when nothing can be filtered. The author's later benchmarks found only modest gains in streaming mode, which is the default, and slowdowns of up to about 7% with many small transactions. The author then asked whether further work was worthwhile, and no reply to that question is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given this, the broader benefit of the patch - especially considering its complexity, may depend on how widely non-streaming mode is used in practice.

precedents_retrieved.title: logical decoding and replication of sequences, take 2
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend logical decoding with a sequence callback, and extend built-in logical replication so publications can include sequences, so that a logical replica's sequences track the primary and do not produce duplicate values after failover. Sequence increments were decoded non-transactionally by default, and transactionally when the sequence's relfilenode was created or altered in an in-progress transaction.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the 2024 'take 2' entry was withdrawn. They do show that an earlier committed version was reverted in April 2022. Review had found that non-transactional sequence changes could be discarded or hit an assertion before the decoding snapshot was consistent, and mixing transactional and non-transactional decoding caused snapshot, abort and streaming problems. The author judged that a fix would need an extensive redesign that was too late for that release cycle, and posted an alternative that WAL-logs sequence state at commit time.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The approach combining transactional and non-transactional behavior implemented by the patch clearly has issues, and it seems foolish to hope we'll find a simple fix.

precedents_retrieved.title: Minimal logical decoding on standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows logical decoding on a hot standby. It adds a catalog-table flag to existing WAL records so the standby can detect snapshot conflicts with logical slots, and it drops conflicting slots, including when wal_level on the primary drops below logical.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the entry was withdrawn. The last messages show the patch set needing repeated rebases and its TAP tests failing intermittently: Rahila Syed reported 018_standby_logical_decoding_xmins.pl failures, and Alvaro Herrera found 019_standby_logical_decoding_conflicts.pl timing out after a rebase in March 2020. No later reply from the author is shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: Filter irrelevant change before reassemble transactions during logical decoding
precedents_retrieved.authors: Jie Li (adger), Ajin Cherian (ajinc), Zhijie Hou (houzj)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch filters out changes to tables that the output plugin will not publish before they are queued in the reorder buffer, so large transactions on unpublished tables do not create spill files. It adds an output plugin callback for filtering by relation, a hash cache of relation file locators, and a rule that pauses filtering for 100 changes after a change that cannot be filtered.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Review was still active when the entry was withdrawn: Shlok Kyal reported a crash with v14-0001, and Ajin Cherian was checking why the patch was faster than HEAD even when all tables were published.

precedents_retrieved.title: Minimal logical decoding on standbys
precedents_retrieved.authors: Andres Freund (andresfreund), Craig Ringer (ringerc), Amit Khandekar (amitdkhan), Ibrar Ahmed (ibrar)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows logical decoding on a physical standby, with catalog-row conflicts on the standby detected from the existing snapshot-conflict WAL records, which gain a flag marking catalog tables. It replaces an earlier design that periodically logged the primary's catalog xmin horizon, and leaves hot_standby_feedback optional.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry died of inactivity. In March 2020 Alvaro Herrera rebased the patch, and its new conflict test then timed out and stopped the test run. No updated version followed, so after six months without updates Michael Paquier returned it with feedback, noting that the patch no longer applied.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
No updates in the last six months, so I am marking it as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Start WAL streaming as early as possible, without waiting for startup process to finish replaying existing WAL. This helps synchronous replication to resume quickly when significant replay lag has been built up.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch starts the WAL receiver on a standby before the startup process finishes replaying WAL already in pg_wal, so synchronous commits on the primary are not held up by replay lag. A GUC, wal_receiver_start_condition, picks when the receiver starts, and the start LSN is the beginning of the most recently flushed segment, found by reading the first page of each segment in pg_wal.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the start LSN is roughly the consistency point, so streaming begins too early when many local segments, often copied by hand, are still left to replay. He also rejected the WAL page checks as hard to maintain, noted that the patch requests streaming when PrimaryConnInfo is not set, and suggested a WAL reader scan from the redo point to find the real end of local WAL. The entry stayed "Waiting on Author" after this review and was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Your patch would cause streaming to begin too early, and a manual copy of segments is not a rare thing as in some environments a bulk copy of segments can make the catchup of a standby faster than streaming.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical decoding of two-phase transactions
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alvaro Herrera, Arseny Sher, Petr Jelinek
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets logical decoding decode a two-phase transaction at PREPARE TRANSACTION time, with output plugin callbacks for prepare, commit prepared and abort prepared. To handle a concurrent ROLLBACK PREPARED during decoding, it first used decode groups that blocked the abort, then later versions stopped decoding when catalog access saw the transaction aborted.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was closed as Returned with feedback because no new patch version was posted after the January 2019 reviews. Those reviews reported open problems, among them that calling SnapBuildCommitTxn at PREPARE makes the catalog changes visible too early. Earlier, in July 2018, Robert Haas questioned whether blocking transaction aborts could work at all, and Andres Freund objected to a planned commit in April 2018.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't understand why this patch record has been kept aliv for so long,
since no new version has been sent in ages.  If this patch is really
waiting on the author, let's see the author do something.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the index search returned no earlier attempt at this idea. In message #2 the author's reply notes that the original thread adding pg_logical_emit_message() decoding has no discussion of the LSN choice, so no earlier rejection reason applies.

No objection from the standards and compatibility angle. The change is a semantic fix with no new syntax, GUC, catalog object or dump state, and the thread settled the main risk by limiting it to master, documenting back branches and flagging it for the release notes (messages #10-#12). The one remaining contract gap, the message_cb text in logicaldecoding.sgml, is already an open request in message #12 and is a documentation fix. The Message LSN field will mean the start LSN for transactional messages and the end LSN for non-transactional ones. Sawada proposed this split and defended it in message #10 on the same ground as commit_lsn and end_lsn, so it follows existing practice. Without the code I could not check that pgoutput and test_decoding emit the new value the same way.

The patch changes the meaning of the Message LSN field, which is part of the replication protocol, but adds no on-disk, WAL, or catalog state. Making it master-only, as settled in messages #10 and #12, keeps old positions valid. A consumer that keeps an old workaround against 20 at worst decodes a change twice. The open items (message_cb docs, a test, the non-transactional case) belong to other angles.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes which LSN, start or end of the same WAL record, is reported to consumers that can already read the slot, so nobody can do or see anything new.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is nothing to object to. The change is a one-line choice in decode.c that core does not use and that adds no hot-path cost, API or GUC. The mixed start/end rule follows the existing commit_lsn/end_lsn practice, and Sawada, a committer who knows the area, shaped the design in message #10 and agreed to own it in message #12. The missing regression test (message #13) and the message_cb text in logicaldecoding.sgml are implementation items. Neither can be checked without the next patch version.

No existing feature, option or extension gives transactional messages a start LSN, so consumers can only compensate in their own code. The patch fixes core behavior to match its documentation, and that cannot move to an extension or hook.

The material shows real demand: Debezium, a widely used CDC connector, lost an INSERT because a transactional message shared the next change's LSN (messages #1, #11), and its maintainers acknowledged the issue (message #7). The fix costs nothing on any hot path, matches the documented behaviour, and reviewers in messages #10 to #13 agree on the master-only scope.
